name: Shoji Miyata
current_role: Founder & CEO, Nstock Inc. (Tokyo); founder of SmartHR (stepped down as CEO 2022, left board 2025)
profile: Japanese entrepreneur who founded KUFU (now SmartHR) in 2013 and launched SmartHR, a cloud HR/labor-management SaaS, in 2015; it became a unicorn after a JPY15.6bn raise in 2021. He handed the CEO role to Masato Serizawa in 2022 and founded Nstock, an equity-compensation SaaS now building a secondary market for private shares.
interesting_fact: Nstock, his second startup, began in 2022 as a wholly owned SmartHR subsidiary and later became independent from the SmartHR Group; it is building a market for trading unlisted startup shares.
deep_cut_fact: Before SmartHR worked, he started a business with a friend in 2013 and racked up more than 10 failed ideas over two years before launching SmartHR in 2015.
notes: Japanese name: 宮田昇始. Best route is via Nstock; the X link is the company account, not his personal one.

name: Brian Barnes
profile: Chicago-born, Stanford economics graduate who did hedge-fund equity research and management consulting before founding M1 Finance in 2015 at about 25. M1 is a 'finance super app' that combines automated investing in user-built 'pies' with borrowing and banking; it has raised more than $300M and reached a unicorn valuation.
interesting_fact: Frustrated by $10 trade commissions and poor tools in his first job after college, he built M1 to automatically route recurring deposits into a user's chosen allocation so no cash sits idle.
deep_cut_fact: He bought his first stock at age 10. After a fifth-grade virtual portfolio contest, his parents opened a real brokerage account in his name on one condition: he had to bring them 'thoughtful research on what to buy and why.'
notes: He has appeared on many podcasts, including Millennial Investing (The Investor's Podcast) and ChooseFI. The press page also lists pr@m1finance.com.

name: Chen Kairan
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Tungee (探迹科技), Guangzhou
profile: Chen Kairan (陈开冉) holds a software-engineering master's from Sun Yat-sen University and was CTO of Jiaxue before co-founding Tungee with CEO Li Zhan in 2016. Tungee sells AI-driven B2B sales SaaS built on a knowledge graph of 100M+ companies and says it has served over 50,000 businesses. He leads its industrial-AI push.
interesting_fact: He built Tungee's two data foundations: the 'Kuanghu' cloud of external industry data (factories, tenders, customs, supply chains) and the 'Taiqing' platform for clients' internal data. Tungee also built ShopGLM, its own e-commerce large model.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Tungee, he did AI research at a university national laboratory and was a researcher on a Ministry of Education-funded data-mining project, specializing in boosting and neural-network algorithms. In 2026 he said: 'Technology itself has no warmth; the warmth lies in the direction of its application.'
notes: Sources call him CTO/co-founder; Li Zhan (黎展) is CEO and the company's public face. The 2026 interview argues for measuring AI by 'token efficiency'. The site lists a general sales hotline and only a recruitment email.

name: Piotr Findeisen
current_role: Co-founder of Starburst; Trino maintainer and Apache DataFusion committer (current employer not confirmed)
profile: Warsaw-based software engineer and founding team member of Starburst, the company behind enterprise Trino (formerly PrestoSQL). He worked on Presto's cost-based optimizer, spill-to-disk and correlated subqueries. He is listed as a Trino maintainer and, more recently, as a committer on the Rust-based Apache DataFusion query engine.
interesting_fact: Before Starburst, he worked at Teradata, where he was the top external committer to Facebook's Presto project, and he was a team leader at the supply-chain SaaS firm Syncron.
deep_cut_fact: He holds an MS in computer science and a BSc in mathematics from the University of Warsaw. Besides Trino, he is now a committer on Apache DataFusion (GitHub: findepi).
notes: Engineer-founder with a low media profile; the open-source communities (Trino Slack/GitHub) are his main public presence. Kasia Findeisen is also a Trino maintainer. I could not confirm whether he still works at Starburst.

name: Joe Wilding
current_role: Co-founder and (per AIAA) Chief Technology Officer, Boom Technology (Boom Supersonic); current title not confirmed
profile: Aerospace engineer who co-founded Boom Supersonic in Denver in 2014 with Blake Scholl and Josh Krall to build the Overture supersonic airliner. He brought decades of certification experience from Hawker Beechcraft, Adam Aircraft, Eclipse Aviation and ICON Aircraft, and has led several passenger aircraft from clean-sheet design through FAA certification.
interesting_fact: He is one of only three Boom co-founders. He has led development of several passenger aircraft from clean-sheet design through FAA certification, the experience Boom needed to certify a new supersonic airliner.
deep_cut_fact: Before Boom, he was Chief Engineer of the Adam A700, a twin-engine very light jet from Adam Aircraft Industries. He was also an early employee at three aerospace startups and worked on experimental and military aircraft projects.
notes: Very low public profile and I found no recent news. I could not confirm whether he is still an active Boom executive; CEO Blake Scholl is the company's public face.

name: Jennifer Bisceglie
current_role: Founder & Executive Vice Chair, Interos (CEO until April 2024)
profile: Supply-chain strategist who founded Interos in 2005 to help federal agencies manage supply-chain risk, then turned it into an AI-driven supply-chain risk and resilience platform valued at about $1B. In April 2024 she handed the CEO role to Ted Krantz and became Founder & Executive Vice Chair. She advises Congress on supply-chain security.
interesting_fact: She was selected as the U.S. delegate to the Women's 20 (W20), the G20 engagement group on gender inequality, and chaired Women Impacting Public Policy (WIPP) from 2010 to 2016.
deep_cut_fact: Her supply-chain career started in retail and footwear: before Interos she worked at Nine West Shoes, American Eagle Outfitters and the logistics software firm Manhattan Associates.
notes: Frequent speaker in national-security and supply-chain circles and media-friendly (Bloomberg, FT, CNBC). She fits an energy/data-center podcast angle on critical-infrastructure supply chains.

name: Shrestha Chowdhury
current_role: Co-founder & CTO, Razor Group (Berlin); current status not confirmed
profile: Co-founder and CTO of Razor Group, a Berlin e-commerce aggregator founded in 2020 that buys and scales Amazon marketplace brands. Razor became a unicorn with a $125M Series B in November 2021. Chowdhury built its data platform for sourcing acquisitions.
interesting_fact: Chowdhury built Razor's 'M&A 2.0' platform, which screened about 1 million companies a week using thousands of data points to flag acquisition targets. Razor said this let it source 99% of its deal pipeline without brokers.
deep_cut_fact: Before Razor, Chowdhury and CEO Tushar Ahluwalia worked on Stalkbuylove, an Indian social-shopping site in the mold of Wanelo.
notes: Very low public profile. TechCrunch (2021) refers to Chowdhury as 'she'. I found no recent coverage, and Razor's leadership has changed since 2024, so confirm the current role before outreach. I found no published press email.

name: Richard Duvall
profile: Co-founder of Zopa, the world's first peer-to-peer lender, launched in 2005 by a team from Egg Banking. Duvall had earlier helped launch Egg at Prudential. He died in 2006 after a battle with cancer.
notes: Deceased (2006), per Peer2Peer Finance News via Alternative Credit Investor: https://alternativecreditinvestor.com/2020/04/28/where-are-they-now-the-p2p-lending-giants-still-run-by-their-founding-members/ . Not a podcast candidate; the other Zopa co-founders (e.g. Giles Andrews) are reachable alternatives.

name: Anurag Arjun
current_role: Co-founder, Avail (modular blockchain data-availability network); co-founder of Polygon (formerly Matic Network)
profile: Indian technologist who co-founded Matic Network (now Polygon) in 2017 with Jaynti Kanani and Sandeep Nailwal and served as its Chief Product Officer. In 2023 he spun Avail, a data-availability project, out of Polygon Labs and became its 'sole steward'. Avail raised a $27M seed round led by Founders Fund and Dragonfly.
interesting_fact: Avail started inside Polygon in late 2020. In March 2023 Polygon spun it off, and Arjun left Polygon Labs to run it as an independent company with co-founder Prabal Banerjee.
deep_cut_fact: Before crypto, he spent years in health-tech product management. At Dexter Consultancy he co-created HealthTrac, a platform that monitored vital signs remotely through wearables, and HealthOne, a free SaaS clinic-management tool for doctors. His first job was programmer analyst at Cognizant in 2006.
notes: Active on X and a regular on crypto podcasts. The deep-cut source is a crowd-edited wiki, so double-check before using it. Hurun lists the wealth source as Polygon Labs.

name: Jose Santacruz
current_role: Payments and fintech engineering leader, Quito (per LinkedIn); former CTO of Kushki. Current employer not confirmed
profile: Ecuadorian engineer who was part of Kushki's founding core team and served as CTO; Kushki became Ecuador's first unicorn. The company's official site lists Aron Schwarzkopf and Sebastián Castro as co-founders, and later sources name a different CTO, so Santacruz has probably moved on.
interesting_fact: In June 2021, as Kushki CTO, he appeared on Thoughtworks' 'Tecnología y Negocios' podcast to talk about taking a company from start-up to scale-up.
deep_cut_fact: He was one of only five people at Kushki, alongside Sebastián Castro, Aron Schwarzkopf, Daniela Espinosa and Melissa Castro, when the payments startup expanded into Colombia in 2019.
notes: I matched him to Kushki as CTO and early team member, but the 'founder' label comes only from Hurun and is not confirmed by Kushki. His current role is unknown, and Kushki publishes no press email (only support/security addresses).

name: Hubert Wong
profile: Software engineer who co-founded CaptivateIQ in 2017 with Mark Schopmeyer and Conway Teng. The no-code platform designs and calculates sales commissions; it went through Y Combinator (Winter 2018) and reached a $1.25B valuation with a $100M raise in January 2022. Wong leads engineering as CTO.
interesting_fact: CaptivateIQ's backers include Sequoia, Accel and Y Combinator. Its January 2022 round valued the commission-software startup at $1.25B less than five years after launch.
notes: Low-profile technical founder; co-CEOs Schopmeyer and Teng are the public faces. Profiles say he was previously a senior software engineer at Vungle, and Comparably adds Amazon and founding engineer at Copilot (acquired by OpenTable), but I could not open those pages to verify.

name: Avery Ching
current_role: Co-founder & CEO, Aptos Labs (CEO since Dec 2024; previously CTO)
profile: Infrastructure engineer who spent more than a decade at Facebook/Meta, where he led batch processing (Spark, Hive/Hadoop, Apache Giraph) and then the crypto platform team behind the Diem blockchain. He co-founded Aptos Labs in 2021 to build a layer-1 blockchain from Diem's open-source technology, launched mainnet in October 2022, and became CEO when Mo Shaikh stepped down in December 2024.
interesting_fact: He testified before the U.S. House Agriculture Committee in June 2025 on digital-asset market structure.
deep_cut_fact: He was born and raised in Honolulu and earned a Northwestern PhD in computer engineering on supercomputing and high-performance file systems. Before Yahoo and Facebook, he built infrastructure at Los Alamos and Sandia national laboratories.
notes: Active on X and frequently speaks at crypto conferences (Consensus, Milken). The HPC/supercomputing background is a natural hook for a data-center podcast.

name: Steven Touw
profile: Steve Touw co-founded Immuta in 2015 with CEO Matthew Carroll and Mike Schiller, all veterans of U.S. intelligence-community data programs. Immuta sells data security and policy-based access-control software for cloud data platforms and became a unicorn. He was previously CTO of 42Six Solutions, which Computer Sciences Corporation (CSC) acquired.
interesting_fact: He designed large-scale geo-temporal analytics for the U.S. intelligence community and Special Operations Command, including some of the very first Hadoop analytics and frameworks for multi-tenant data-policy controls, the ideas behind Immuta.
deep_cut_fact: His academic background is in geography rather than computer science (University of Maryland, B.S. Geography), and he has been described as a former geospatial analyst, which led to his geo-temporal analytics work.
notes: Writes bylined articles on data security (RTInsights, Solutions Review). The geography/NGA detail came only from search summaries of profile sites and has no verified URL, so treat the deep cut as unconfirmed. I found no published press email.
